detailed_rationale:
TVS Supply Chain Solutions Ltd provides integrated supply-chain management and logistics services to large enterprises and government departments internationally. Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 3,032 crore but net profit was only Rs 18 crore, a razor-thin 0.6% net margin, though this does represent a real turnaround from a loss-making recent past (TTM profit growth of over 1,000%, entirely a base effect of moving from losses to a small profit and not indicative of a durable, high-margin business model). Three-year sales growth of just 3% shows the top line has been essentially flat over that window.

Governance and structural factors are the more serious concerns here. Promoter pledge stands at 31.9% -- a real, material governance red flag for an existing-holdings review, since it creates a forced-selling risk independent of the company's operating performance. The company is also mid-way through an NCLT-approved amalgamation of five transferor companies (Bengaluru NCLT approval still pending as of the latest update), a corporate restructuring that will make historical financial comparisons less reliable for a period and could either simplify the group (positive) or introduce further one-off adjustments that obscure the true run-rate (a real risk given how thin current margins already are).

Reverse-DCF: 32.3x earnings for a 0.6% net margin business with a flat top line, high promoter pledge and a pending multi-entity merger is not attractively priced for the risk being taken. The recently 'positive' profit and 'high' one-year return metrics reflect a low-base turnaround, not demonstrated durable profitability, and I don't think it is safe to extrapolate them forward. I side with the quant Sell, and the pledge level alone would keep me cautious on this name regardless of the operating numbers.
recommendation_rationale: The company has only just turned profitable, and at a razor-thin 0.6% net margin, on essentially flat (3% three-year) revenue growth; the sharp headline profit-growth number is a low-base artifact, not evidence of a durable margin structure. A 31.9% promoter pledge is a genuine governance red flag on its own, and a pending five-entity merger adds further uncertainty to reading the true run-rate. Sell.
summary: TVS Supply Chain Solutions has recently turned profitable after a period of losses, but its profit margin remains extremely thin and revenue growth has been essentially flat over the past three years. The company also carries a meaningfully pledged promoter stake and is in the middle of a multi-entity merger that adds further uncertainty to its numbers. We rate this a Sell given the combination of thin margins, a governance flag, and limited visibility into the post-merger run-rate.
positive_para: The company has genuinely turned the corner from losses to profit, operates in a growing outsourced-logistics/supply-chain category serving large enterprise and government clients internationally, and its working-capital cycle is favourably negative (-21 days), an efficient structural feature of the business model.
negative_para: Net margin remains razor-thin at 0.6%, three-year revenue growth has been essentially flat (3%), and the sharp headline profit-growth figure is simply a low-base effect from moving out of losses rather than a sign of durable earnings power. A 31.9% promoter pledge is a real governance concern, and the ongoing NCLT-approved amalgamation of five group entities adds further uncertainty to reading the company's true underlying run-rate for a period.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A 32.3x P/E for a 0.6%-net-margin business with flat revenue growth, a meaningfully pledged promoter stake, and a pending multi-entity merger is not attractively priced for the risk involved. The apparently strong one-year profit growth is a low-base turnaround artifact rather than evidence of durable profitability, and should not be extrapolated forward.
